review: 603.2h-1: Morbid Opportunist's 'This ability triggers only once each turn' is not the 'Do this only once each turn' wording 603.2h governs, and the scenario could not show the rule's point that a declined action leaves the ability able to trigger again; rewrote it with Ancient Cornucopia, Grizzly Bears and Watchwolf, base accepting the first gain and the variant declining it.
603.2g-1: decisions did not resolve Jackal Pup's trigger, which the base outcome needs; added the step.
603.6d-1: the variant's delta chose a target for a trigger that never triggers; removed the targeting clause.
603.7-1: B's library was empty and the scenario passes through B's draw step, so B would lose the game; gave B three Islands in library.
603.7a-1: the end-step variant plays through B's draw step with B's library empty, so B would lose the game; gave B three Islands in library.
603.7c-1: the bounced-and-recast variant changed two facts at once (a bounce, then a recast); replaced it with a one-action Cloudshift flicker, with Plains replacing the two Forests.
603.9, 603.10f: removed from skipped and reclassified as out_of_scope in the triage, since their own skip reason says they cannot occur in a two-player Forge game.

603.7g: the skip reason claimed no Forge card has this shape, but dash and blitz are static abilities allowing an action that creates a delayed trigger; rewrote the reason around the fact that no reachable state changes the source or controller.

skipped.reason: cannot be illustrated: no card in Forge's cardsfolder has a triggered ability that carries a 'this ability can't be countered' or targeting-limit instruction after its effect (Spider-Punk's 'abilities can't be countered' is a static ability, which is a different rule)
cannot be illustrated: no card in Forge's cardsfolder has a triggered ability with several trigger conditions and an instruction about whether 'all' of them occurred
cannot be illustrated with a Forge state: a triggered ability whose source is never visible to all players needs a hidden-zone source with a trigger, which no Forge card script models
cannot be illustrated: no card in Forge's cardsfolder has a static ability whose replacement effect creates a delayed triggered ability

no state flips what this rule decides: the Forge mechanics of this shape, such as dash and blitz, put the static ability on the card being cast, so the delayed trigger's source and controller are that permanent and its caster in every reachable case, and its effect does not depend on who controls it

cannot be illustrated: no card in Forge's cardsfolder creates a delayed trigger that counts the resolutions of its creating ability; Ashling the Pilgrim and Ashling, Flame Dancer count resolutions inside the ability instead

scenarios.title: A triggered ability triggers when its trigger event happens and does nothing until it resolves
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests.
Both players pass; Grizzly Bears resolves and enters the battlefield.
Soul Warden's triggered ability goes on the stack the next time a player would receive priority; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Soul Warden triggers exactly once when Grizzly Bears enters; the trigger has changed nothing (A's life is 20) until it resolves, and after it resolves A's life is 21.

variants.label: land-instead
variants.delta: A plays Forest from hand instead of casting Grizzly Bears (a land, not a creature, enters).
variants.expected: Soul Warden does not trigger and nothing goes on the stack; A's life stays 20.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A plays Forest from hand instead of casting Grizzly Bears

detector.outcome: A zone-change trigger for a permanent entering the battlefield is evaluated against the entering event and fires.

A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests. Both players pass; Grizzly Bears resolves.
B's Soul Warden trigger goes on the stack; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: B's Soul Warden triggers although B can't cast spells this turn; B's life is 21.

variants.label: land-instead
variants.delta: After Silence resolves, A plays Forest from hand instead of casting Grizzly Bears.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A plays Forest instead of casting Grizzly Bears

scenarios.title: All abilities that trigger at the beginning of a step trigger when it begins

setup.notes: The upkeep has just begun; abilities that trigger at the beginning of it have not yet been put on the stack. In the variant the active player is B and B's upkeep has just begun.

decisions: A's upkeep begins. Both Phyrexian Arena abilities trigger and A puts them on the stack in either order.
Both players pass until both abilities have resolved.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Both Phyrexian Arenas trigger as the upkeep begins; A draws 2 cards and loses 2 life (life 18).

variants.delta: It is B's upkeep (B is the active player), not A's.

detector.outcome: A beginning-of-step trigger is evaluated as that step begins and fires.
detector.near_miss: The same kind of trigger is evaluated at a step it does not name and does not fire.

scenarios.title: A 'becomes tapped' trigger fires for a permanent that changes from untapped to tapped but not for one that enters tapped
decisions: B plays Temple Garden and pays 2 life, so it enters untapped (B's life 18).
B taps Temple Garden for mana (the mana is not used). Lifetap's trigger goes on the stack; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Temple Garden (a Forest) becomes tapped, so Lifetap triggers once; A's life is 21.

variants.label: enters-tapped
variants.delta: B does not pay the 2 life, so Temple Garden enters tapped, and B does not tap it afterwards.
variants.expected: Temple Garden enters tapped; it never becomes tapped, so Lifetap does not trigger; A's life stays 20 and B's life stays 20.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B declines to pay 2 life for Temple Garden

detector.outcome: A becomes-tapped trigger is evaluated when an untapped permanent becomes tapped and fires.
detector.near_miss: A becomes-tapped trigger evaluated against a permanent becoming tapped that its condition does not match does not fire; a permanent that enters tapped never becomes tapped, so no such trigger is evaluated for it.

scenarios.title: A prevented event does not trigger anything
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Jackal Pup, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.
Jackal Pup's trigger goes on the stack if it triggered; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Shock deals 2 damage to Jackal Pup (2/1); Jackal Pup's ability triggers and deals 2 damage to B (life 18); Jackal Pup dies.

variants.label: damage-prevented
variants.delta: After A casts Shock, B responds with Healing Salve choosing the prevention mode targeting Jackal Pup, tapping Plains; Healing Salve resolves first, then Shock resolves.
variants.expected: Healing Salve's shield prevents all 2 damage from Shock, so Jackal Pup is not dealt damage and its ability does not trigger; Jackal Pup stays on the battlefield undamaged and B's life stays 20.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B responds with Healing Salve choosing the prevention mode

scenarios.forge_notes: Jackal Pup dies to the damage in the base variant; its trigger still happens because it triggers as the damage is dealt.

detector.outcome: A damage-dealt trigger is evaluated against damage actually dealt and fires.
detector.near_miss: A damage-dealt trigger evaluated against dealt damage its condition does not match does not fire; damage that was prevented is never dealt, so no such trigger is evaluated for it.

scenarios.title: An ability with 'Do this only once each turn' triggers again only if its controller has not yet taken the action this turn
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping two Forests. Ancient Cornucopia triggers; both players pass and the trigger resolves; A chooses to gain life.
Both players pass; Grizzly Bears resolves.
A casts Watchwolf, tapping the third Forest and Plains. If Ancient Cornucopia triggers, A chooses to gain life when it resolves; both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Ancient Cornucopia triggers on Grizzly Bears and A gains 1 life (life 21); it does not trigger on Watchwolf because A has already gained life with it this turn; A's life stays 21.

variants.label: declined-first
variants.delta: When the first Ancient Cornucopia trigger resolves, A chooses not to gain life.
variants.expected: A gains nothing from the first trigger; Ancient Cornucopia triggers again on Watchwolf (green and white) and A gains 2 life (life 22).

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A chooses not to gain life when the trigger resolves

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge scripts the clause as ResolvedLimit$ 1 on the trigger; check that a resolution where the optional gain was declined does not count toward the limit.

detector.outcome: A cast trigger limited to once each turn is evaluated and fires when its action has not yet been taken this turn.
detector.near_miss: The same trigger evaluated after the limited action was taken this turn does not fire.

scenarios.title: A triggered ability goes on the stack as the topmost object, where it can be responded to
decisions: A casts Shock targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain. Kor Firewalker's trigger goes on the stack above Shock.
Both players pass; the trigger resolves and A chooses to gain 1 life.
Both players pass; Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The trigger is on top of Shock and resolves first: A's life is 21 before Shock resolves; then Shock resolves and Grizzly Bears (2/2) dies.

variants.label: stifled
variants.delta: With the trigger on the stack, B responds with Stifle targeting Kor Firewalker's trigger, tapping Island.
variants.expected: Stifle counters the trigger, so A gains no life (life stays 20); Shock then resolves and Grizzly Bears dies.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B responds with Stifle targeting the trigger

scenarios.title: A triggered ability is controlled by whoever controlled its source when it triggered
decisions: A casts Act of Treason targeting Soul Warden, tapping three Mountains. Both players pass; it resolves and A gains control of Soul Warden until end of turn.
A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests. Both players pass; it resolves.
Soul Warden's trigger goes on the stack; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Soul Warden's trigger is controlled by A, who controlled Soul Warden when it triggered: A's life is 21 and B's life stays 20.

variants.label: no-steal
variants.delta: A does not cast Act of Treason; A only casts Grizzly Bears, so B still controls Soul Warden.
variants.expected: Soul Warden's trigger is controlled by B: B's life is 21 and A's life stays 20.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A does not cast Act of Treason

detector.outcome: A zone-change trigger for a permanent entering the battlefield is evaluated against the entering event and fires.
detector.near_miss: The same kind of trigger is evaluated against an event and does not fire.

scenarios.title: A modal triggered ability with no legal mode to choose is removed from the stack
decisions: A casts Downwind Ambusher, tapping four Swamps. Both players pass; it resolves.
Its enters trigger is put on the stack: A chooses the mode 'Target creature an opponent controls gets -1/-1 until end of turn' targeting Savannah Lions, if that mode is legal.
Both players pass; the trigger resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The -1/-1 mode is legal (the 'destroy a damaged creature' mode is not, since Savannah Lions is undamaged); Savannah Lions (2/1) gets -1/-1 and dies.

variants.label: no-opposing-creature
variants.delta: B controls no creatures (Savannah Lions is not on the battlefield).
variants.expected: Neither mode has a legal target, so no mode can be chosen and the trigger is removed from the stack; nothing happens and Downwind Ambusher stays on the battlefield.

detector.none: A modal trigger with no legal mode is never put on the stack: the trigger record shows only fired=true, and no resolution record or event is written for an ability removed before resolving, so nothing shows the removal.

scenarios.title: A triggered ability with no legal choices is removed from the stack
decisions: A casts Nekrataal, tapping four Swamps. Both players pass; it resolves.
Its enters trigger is put on the stack targeting a nonartifact, nonblack creature if there is one.
Both players pass; the trigger resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The trigger targets Grizzly Bears and destroys it; Grizzly Bears moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: only-black-creature
variants.delta: B's creature is Walking Corpse (a black 2/2) instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: No nonblack, nonartifact creature can be targeted (Nekrataal itself is black), so the trigger is removed from the stack without resolving; Walking Corpse stays on the battlefield.

detector.none: A trigger with no legal target is removed without going on the stack: the trigger record shows only fired=true, and no resolution record or event is written for it (a fizzle outcome is for an ability that was on the stack), so nothing shows the removal.

scenarios.title: An intervening 'if' clause is checked when the trigger event occurs and again on resolution

setup.notes: In the one-life-short variant A's life is 39. A's upkeep has just begun.

decisions: A's upkeep begins and Felidar Sovereign's condition (40 or more life) is checked.
If it triggers, both players pass and the ability resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: A has 40 life when the upkeep begins, so the ability triggers; it still holds 40 life on resolution, and A wins the game.

variants.label: life-lost-in-response
variants.delta: With the trigger on the stack, B casts Shock targeting A (tapping Mountain); Shock resolves first, A's life becomes 38.
variants.expected: The ability triggered, but on resolution A has 38 life, so it is removed from the stack and does nothing; A does not win and A's life is 38.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B casts Shock targeting A in response

variants.label: one-life-short
variants.delta: A's life total is 39 as the upkeep begins.
variants.expected: The ability does not trigger and nothing goes on the stack; A does not win and A's life stays 39.

scenarios.forge_notes: Check that Forge re-evaluates LifeTotal/LifeAmount on resolution (intervening if).

detector.outcome: A beginning-of-step trigger with an intervening if clause is evaluated as the step begins and fires when the condition holds.

scenarios.title: A zone-change trigger cannot find its object if the object left the zone it moved to

scenarios.title: An Aura's trigger on the enchanted creature dying finds the Aura's new object in the graveyard

scenarios.title: A spell creates a delayed triggered ability that triggers once, later, and is controlled by the spell's controller
decisions: A casts Flare targeting B, tapping three Mountains. Both players pass; Flare resolves, dealing 1 damage to B and creating the delayed ability.

detector.outcome: A delayed triggered ability created by a resolving spell or ability is evaluated when its event occurs and fires.

scenarios.title: A delayed triggered ability does not trigger on an event that happened before it was created

variants.label: larger-creature
variants.delta: A's other creature is Centaur Courser (3/3) instead of Grizzly Bears.
variants.expected: Shock leaves Centaur Courser on the battlefield with 2 damage marked; A still controls another creature, so Emperor Crocodile does not trigger and stays on the battlefield.

detector.outcome: A state trigger is evaluated while the game state matches its condition and fires once, not again while it is on the stack.
detector.near_miss: The same state trigger evaluated while its condition does not hold, or while it is already on the stack, does not fire.

scenarios.title: A leaves-the-battlefield trigger looks back in time, so a permanent destroyed together with creatures still triggers
decisions: A activates Nevinyrral's Disk, paying {1} with Swamp and tapping the Disk. Both players pass; the ability resolves and destroys all artifacts, creatures and enchantments at once.
Bastion of Remembrance's triggers go on the stack; both players pass until they have resolved.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Bastion of Remembrance is destroyed at the same time as the two Grizzly Bears but still triggers once for each Bears; B loses 2 life (life 18) and A gains 2 life (life 22).

variants.label: bastion-gone
variants.delta: Bastion of Remembrance is in A's graveyard instead of on the battlefield.
variants.expected: The two Grizzly Bears die with no Bastion of Remembrance to trigger; life totals stay 20 and 20.

operation.unclassifiable: more than one fact: Bastion of Remembrance leaves the battlefield and sits in A's graveyard (a removal plus a move)

detector.outcome: A leaves-the-battlefield trigger of a permanent leaving at the same time as the permanents it watches is evaluated looking back in time and fires.
detector.near_miss: A dies trigger evaluated against a battlefield-to-graveyard move its condition does not match does not fire.

scenarios.title: An ability that triggers when a permanent phases out looks back in time

setup.notes: In the base variant the Imp is phased out. The variant's step is B's upkeep.

decisions: Teferi's Imp has phased out during A's untap step, which has just ended, and its 'whenever phases out' ability is waiting to be put on the stack.
Both players pass; the ability resolves and A discards a card.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Teferi's Imp is phased out when the ability triggers, but the ability still triggers; A discards Island (hand empty).

variants.label: opponent-turn
variants.delta: It is B's upkeep (B is the active player) and Teferi's Imp is phased in on A's battlefield.
variants.expected: Teferi's Imp does not phase out on B's untap step; its ability does not trigger and A's hand stays Island.

operation.unclassifiable: phase or turn: it is B's upkeep and B is the active player

scenarios.forge_notes: The phased-out state of a permanent set up before the upkeep may need to be reached by playing through the untap step.

detector.outcome: A phases-out trigger is evaluated as its permanent phases out and fires.
detector.near_miss: The same trigger evaluated against a permanent that is not phasing out does not fire.

scenarios.title: An ability that triggers when an object becomes unattached looks back in time
decisions: A passes priority with an empty stack.
B casts Shatter targeting Grafted Wargear, tapping both Mountains. Both players pass; it resolves and Grafted Wargear is destroyed.
The Wargear's 'becomes unattached' trigger goes on the stack if it triggered; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grafted Wargear becomes unattached as it leaves the battlefield and its trigger still triggers; A sacrifices Grizzly Bears, which moves to A's graveyard.

variants.label: not-attached
variants.delta: Grafted Wargear is not attached to Grizzly Bears (it is unattached on the battlefield).
variants.expected: Grafted Wargear is destroyed without becoming unattached from anything; no trigger; Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield.

operation.unclassifiable: not a board edit: the attachment of Grafted Wargear to Grizzly Bears, which no operation sets

detector.outcome: An unattached trigger is evaluated as an attached object becomes unattached and fires.
detector.near_miss: The same trigger evaluated for an object that was not attached does not fire.

scenarios.title: An ability that triggers when a player loses control of an object looks back in time
decisions: A activates Coffin Queen ({2}{B}, {T}) targeting Grizzly Bears in A's graveyard. Both players pass; it resolves and Grizzly Bears enters under A's control.
A passes priority. B casts Shock targeting Coffin Queen, tapping Mountain. Both players pass; Shock resolves and Coffin Queen (1/1) dies.
Coffin Queen's 'when you lose control of Coffin Queen' ability goes on the stack if it triggered; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: A loses control of Coffin Queen as it leaves the battlefield and the ability still triggers; Grizzly Bears is exiled.

variants.label: shock-the-creature
variants.delta: B's Shock targets Grizzly Bears instead of Coffin Queen.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears dies and goes to A's graveyard; A keeps control of Coffin Queen, so nothing is exiled.

operation.unclassifiable: target: B's Shock targets Grizzly Bears instead of Coffin Queen

detector.outcome: A loses-control trigger is evaluated as a permanent leaves its controller's control and fires, looking back in time.
detector.near_miss: The same trigger evaluated when the permanent does not leave its controller's control does not fire.

scenarios.title: An ability that triggers when a spell is countered triggers when its spell is countered
decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping both Forests.
B responds with Counterspell targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping both Islands. Both players pass; Counterspell resolves and counters Grizzly Bears.
Multani's Presence's trigger goes on the stack if it triggered; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is countered and goes to A's graveyard; Multani's Presence triggers and A draws 1 card.

variants.label: not-countered
variants.delta: B does not cast Counterspell.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears resolves and enters the battlefield; Multani's Presence does not trigger and A draws nothing.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: B does not cast Counterspell

scenarios.forge_notes: Multani's Presence is a permanent, so this does not stress the look-back part of the rule on its own; it covers the trigger on a countered spell.

detector.outcome: A spell-countered trigger is evaluated as a spell is countered and fires.
detector.near_miss: The same kind of trigger evaluated against a countered spell or ability its condition does not match does not fire.

scenarios.title: A reflexive triggered ability triggers only if the stated action happened during the resolution that created it
decisions: A casts Heart-Piercer Manticore, tapping four Mountains. Both players pass; it resolves.
Its enters trigger goes on the stack and resolves: A may sacrifice another creature; A chooses to sacrifice Grizzly Bears.
The reflexive trigger triggers; A targets Savannah Lions; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is sacrificed, the reflexive 'when you do' ability triggers and Heart-Piercer Manticore deals 2 damage (Grizzly Bears's power) to Savannah Lions, which dies.

variants.label: declined
variants.delta: A chooses not to sacrifice a creature.
variants.expected: No creature is sacrificed, so the reflexive ability does not trigger; Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield and Savannah Lions takes no damage.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A chooses not to sacrifice a creature

detector.outcome: A reflexive 'when you do' triggered ability created during a resolution is evaluated and fires.
detector.near_miss: A reflexive triggered ability is evaluated and does not fire.

scenarios.title: Paying a cost several times makes a reflexive triggered ability trigger only once
decisions: A attacks with Nyssa of Traken. Its attack trigger goes on the stack; both players pass and it resolves.
On resolution A sacrifices both Mishra's Baubles as the cost. The 'when you sacrifice one or more artifacts this way' ability triggers.
A targets both Grizzly Bears with it; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The reflexive ability triggers once, not once per artifact: both Grizzly Bears become tapped and A draws 2 cards.

variants.label: none-sacrificed
variants.delta: A sacrifices no artifacts.
variants.expected: The reflexive ability does not trigger; neither Grizzly Bears is tapped and A draws no cards.

operation.unclassifiable: choice: A sacrifices no artifacts

detector.outcome: A reflexive triggered ability fires once for its creating resolution.
detector.near_miss: A reflexive triggered ability is evaluated and does not fire.
